text: Again I looked up, and there before me was a flying scroll.
He asked me, "What do you see?" I answered, "I see a flying scroll, twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide."

Then he said to me, "This is the curse going out over the whole land. According to one side of the scroll, every thief will be swept away; according to the other, everyone who swears falsely will be swept away.

I am sending it out, declares the LORD of hosts, and it will enter the house of the thief and the house of the one who swears falsely by my name. It will remain in his house and consume it, both its timbers and its stones."
Then the angel who was speaking with me came forward and said, "Look up and see what this is that is going out."
I asked, "What is it?" He answered, "It is a measuring basket going out." And he added, "This is their iniquity in all the land."

versions.text: I asked, "What is it?" He answered, "It is a measuring basket going out." And he added, "This is the iniquity of the whole land."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew pronoun suffix ("their") is dropped in the current rendering. Also, the Hebrew text as preserved reads "their eye"; "iniquity" follows the ancient versions. A footnote is warranted: "Hebrew reads 'their eye'; some ancient versions read 'their iniquity.'"

text: Then the lead cover was lifted, and there sat a woman inside the basket.
He said, "This is Wickedness," and he pushed her back into the basket and slammed the lead cover down over its mouth.
Then I looked up, and there before me were two women coming, with the wind in their wings. Their wings were like those of a stork, and they lifted the basket and carried it between earth and sky.
"Where are they taking the basket?" I asked the angel who was speaking with me.

He answered, "To build a house for it in the land of Shinar.[^1] When the house is ready, the basket will be set there on its pedestal."

[^1]: Shinar: the ancient name for the region of Babylonia (see Genesis 11:2).

versions.text: He answered, "To the land of Babylonia, to build a house for it. When the house is ready, the basket will be set there on its pedestal."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has שִׁנְעָר (Shinar), the ancient name evoking Babel/Babylon (cf. Genesis 11:2). Rendering it as "Babylonia" removes the deliberate allusion; keep "Shinar" and add a footnote such as: "Shinar: the region of Babylonia."

versions.text: He answered, "To the land of Shinar, to build a house for it. When the house is ready, the basket will be set there on its pedestal."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew word order leads with the purpose ("to build a house for it") and names Shinar as the location; keeping that order follows the source more closely and still reads smoothly aloud. A brief footnote on "Shinar" is worth adding, since the proper name alone may not communicate the Babylon allusion to a listener; no footnote appears to be attached yet.
